# Introduction

This document describes how to use AlphaSimR to model
genotype-by-environment interaction.

**This article is a draft of a planned interface, which AlphaSimR does
not provide yet.** The `legacyGxE`, `varGxL` and `varGxL_Y` arguments of
`addTraitAG`, the `useGxE` argument of `setVarE`, and the `year`, `locs`
and `returnPheno` arguments of `setPheno` do not exist, so the code below
is not run and would not work as written. Of the calls shown, only the
first `setPheno` call, which sets the environment with `p`, works now. GxE
traits are currently added with the `varGxE` and `varEnv` arguments of
`addTraitAG`, `addTraitADG`, `addTraitAEG` and `addTraitADEG`, as described
in `vignette("traits")`.

```{r, eval=FALSE}

# Legacy GxE trait
SP$addTraitAG(nQtlPerChr=100, mean=0, var=1, varGxE=1, legacyGxE=TRUE)

# New GxE trait
SP$addTraitAG(nQtlPerChr=100, mean=0, var=1, varGxL=1, varGxL_Y=1)

SP$setVarE(H2=0.5, useGxE=TRUE)

# Legacy GxE
p = runif(40)
year = 1
pop = setPheno(pop, p=p[year], reps=2, fixEff=year)

# New GxE trait
year = 1
pop = setPheno(pop, year=year, reps=1, locs=2)

PYT = setPheno(PYT, year=year, fixEff=paste0("PYT_", year))

pheno_df = setPheno(PYT, year=year, fixEff=paste0("PYT_", year), returnPheno=TRUE)
```

# Decisions to make

The new model is meant to give a compound symmetry covariance between
environments by sampling additive QTL deviations for each environment
inside `setPheno`, with the year's deviations reproducible from a seed
and the locations' deviations sampled at random. The questions below have
to be settled before the interface above can be implemented or
documented. Each one ends with an empty chunk for the proposed code.

## 1. The model and the meaning of each variance

The article needs the model written out, for example
$y = \mu + g + (gY) + (gL{\cdot}Y) + e$, with the variance each argument
sets and the covariance it implies between two records of the same
genotype. What do `varGxL` and `varGxL_Y` stand for? Is `varGxL` a
location deviation that persists across years, or is it specific to a
location in one year? Is `varGxL_Y` genotype by year, or location within
year? If locations are sampled afresh on every call, a persistent
genotype by location term cannot exist, and the variance drawn per
location is really a location-year term.

```{r, eval=FALSE}

```

## 2. How a year is identified

The plan uses `p` as the seed for the year deviations, but the code above
uses a `year` argument. A `p` is a floating point value, so `p[year]` and a
typed constant can differ in the last bits and give different effects, and
`p` already means the quantile of the environmental covariate for legacy
traits. An integer `year` avoids both. Should the year be identified by
`p` or by an integer `year`?

If the seed is derived from the year alone, every replicate of a
simulation draws the same year deviations, even after different calls to
`set.seed()`, which correlates the replicates without warning. Should the
`SimParam` hold a random salt, drawn when it is created or when the trait
is added, that is combined with the year?

```{r, eval=FALSE}

```

## 3. How a location is identified

With `locs=2` sampling two new locations on every call, two trials in the
same year never share a site, and no location can be followed across
years. Is that intended? Should `locs` also accept a vector of location
identifiers, seeded like years, so that trials can share sites and a
target population of environments can be modeled?

```{r, eval=FALSE}

```

## 4. How `reps` and `locs` combine

Is the phenotype an entry mean over locations and replicates, so that the
error variance is divided by `locs * reps` and the location variance by
`locs`? Can `reps` differ between locations? Are plot-level records
available, and if so through which argument?

```{r, eval=FALSE}

```

## 5. What `returnPheno` returns

`setPheno` already has `onlyPheno`, which returns the phenotype matrix
instead of the population. How does `returnPheno` differ from it? If it
returns a data frame, which columns does it carry (for example id, trait,
year, location, replicate and value), and does it still update the
population?

```{r, eval=FALSE}

```

## 6. What `H2` and `h2` mean with `useGxE=TRUE`

Which variances enter the denominator of `setVarE(H2=0.5, useGxE=TRUE)`,
and is the heritability on a plot basis or an entry-mean basis? The same
question applies to the `h2` and `H2` arguments of `setPheno`.

```{r, eval=FALSE}

```

## 7. What `gv` holds for a new GxE trait

Is `gv`, and so `bv`, `genParam` and selection on `"gv"`, the main effect
only, that is the mean over the target population of environments? Are
the variances of the GxE terms reported anywhere, such as in `genParam`,
and are they computed from the current population or fixed at the
founders?

```{r, eval=FALSE}

```

## 8. The type of `fixEff`

`fixEff=paste0("PYT_", year)` is a string, but `setPheno` stores
`as.integer(fixEff)`, which turns a string into `NA` with a warning. Does
the `fixEff` slot become character or factor, and what does that change in
the genomic and pedigree prediction models that read it?

```{r, eval=FALSE}

```

## 9. Which traits and populations are covered

Is the new model offered only through `addTraitAG`, or also through
`addTraitADG`, `addTraitAEG` and `addTraitADEG`? With several traits, are
the GxE deviations correlated between traits, and through which argument?
Which of `HybridPop`, `MultiPop`, `setPhenoGCA` and `setPhenoProgTest`
support it?

```{r, eval=FALSE}

```

## 10. Legacy and new traits together

What is the default of `legacyGxE`? If it is `FALSE`, every existing
script that adds a GxE trait changes its results, which is a change to
results from a seed. Can one `SimParam` hold legacy and new GxE traits,
and what do `p` and `year` do in a `setPheno` call that phenotypes both?

```{r, eval=FALSE}

```

## 11. Random number streams

Which draws come from the seeded year generator, which from R's stream,
and which from the C++ substreams? The year deviations should consume
nothing from R's stream, so that adding a phenotyping call does not move
later results, and none of the draws may depend on `nThreads`.

```{r, eval=FALSE}

```

## 12. Drawing or storing the deviations

Are the deviations for a year drawn again on every call, which keeps the
`SimParam` free of state but repeats the work, or drawn once and stored on
the trait? If they are stored, how are they kept when the `SimParam` is
saved, and how are they discarded?

```{r, eval=FALSE}

```
